category: CFD/Microfluidics: Multiphase Flow (Level Set, Phase Field, Moving Mesh, Bubbly, Mixture, Euler-Euler, Phase Transport)
description: Multiphase flow interfaces and features of the CFD, Microfluidics, Polymer Flow and Mixer Modules: interface-tracking methods (level set, phase field, ternary phase field, moving mesh), dispersed-flow models (bubbly flow, mixture model, Euler-Euler, phase transport mixture model), phase transport in porous media and the multiphysics couplings that tie them to the flow interfaces, with verified Java type strings (COMSOL 6.4).

tools.name: Turbulent Two-Phase Flow, Level Set (multiphysics interfaces)
tools.description: Predefined multiphysics interfaces that combine a Turbulent Flow interface (Algebraic yPlus, L-VEL, k-ε, realizable k-ε, k-ω, SST, low-Re k-ε, Spalart–Allmaras or v2-f) with a Level Set interface and the Two-Phase Flow, Level Set coupling. They track a sharp interface between two immiscible fluids at high Reynolds number, for example free surfaces in stirred tanks, sloshing and spillways. Simulations are always time dependent.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Multiphase Flow > Two-Phase Flow, Level Set > Turbulent Two-Phase Flow, Level Set > (k-ε, SST, ...); Java: physics().create("spf", "TurbulentFlowkeps", "geom1"); physics().create("ls", "LevelSet", "geom1"); multiphysics().create("tpf1", "TwoPhaseFlowLevelSet", 3)

parameters.name: Turbulence model
parameters.description: Chosen by the menu entry; wall functions or automatic wall treatment.

parameters.name: Discretization
parameters.description: Default P1+P1 flow and linear level set.

parameters.name: Study
parameters.description: Time Dependent with Phase Initialization (plus Wall Distance Initialization for models that need it).

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. The laminar variant (Laminar Two-Phase Flow, Level Set) is available with the Microfluidics Module too.

tools.name: Two-Phase Flow, Level Set (Multiphysics Coupling)
tools.description: Coupling feature (default name tpf1) that makes the flow interface use density and viscosity averaged by the level set volume fraction, adds the surface tension force as a volume force, and lets the Level Set interface convect the interface with the computed velocity. Fluid properties per phase come from materials, a Multiphase Material, non-Newtonian models or user expressions.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Two-Phase Flow, Level Set; Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("tpf1", "TwoPhaseFlowLevelSet", 3)

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Fluid flow (spf) and Moving interface (ls).

parameters.name: Material properties
parameters.description: Locally defined (Fluid 1/Fluid 2 density and viscosity) or from a Multiphase Material.

parameters.name: Surface tension
parameters.description: Include surface tension force; coefficient user defined or from the library (water/air, oil/water, ...).

parameters.name: Non-Newtonian fluids
parameters.description: Power law, Carreau, Bingham/Herschel–Bulkley/Casson–Papanastasiou per phase.

tools.notes: Verified type string TwoPhaseFlowLevelSet. For incompressible fluids, density dependencies on T and p are replaced by reference values.

tools.name: Wetted Wall (Multiphysics Coupling)
tools.description: Boundary coupling for walls in contact with a moving fluid-fluid interface: it replaces the flow Wall and the level set No Flow conditions with no penetration plus a Navier-slip tangential stress (slip length β ≈ mesh size) so the contact line can move, and adds the force that enforces the contact angle when surface tension is included. The contact angle is given directly or from Young's equation.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Wetted Wall (boundary); Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("ww1", "WettedWall", 2)

parameters.name: Contact angle θw
parameters.description: Angle between interface and wall, or computed from surface energies (Young's equation).

parameters.name: Slip length β
parameters.description: Default related to the mesh element size.

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Flow interface and Level Set (or Phase Field) interface.

tools.notes: Available for laminar flow and turbulent flow with wall functions/automatic wall treatment. The contact angle is not enforced on boundaries adjacent to porous domains.

tools.name: Interior Wetted Wall (Multiphysics Coupling)
tools.description: Interior-boundary version of the Wetted Wall coupling acting on both sides of thin walls, allowing velocity, pressure, level set and turbulence discontinuities across the boundary. It lets thin plates and membranes in contact with a moving interface be modeled without meshing their thickness.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Interior Wetted Wall; Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("iww1", "InteriorWettedWall", 2)

parameters.name: Contact angle
parameters.description: Applied on both sides.

parameters.name: Slip length
parameters.description: Navier slip length for laminar flow.

tools.notes: Overrides the flow Interior Wall and the level set Thin Barrier on its selection.

tools.name: Turbulent Two-Phase Flow, Phase Field (multiphysics interfaces)
tools.description: Predefined interfaces combining a Turbulent Flow interface with the Phase Field in Fluids interface and the Two-Phase Flow, Phase Field coupling. The Cahn–Hilliard phase field gives a thermodynamically consistent diffuse interface with built-in surface tension, suited for free surfaces and dispersed droplets at higher Reynolds numbers.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Multiphase Flow > Two-Phase Flow, Phase Field > Turbulent Two-Phase Flow, Phase Field > (k-ε, SST, ...); Java: physics().create("pf", "PhaseField", "geom1"); multiphysics().create("tpf1", "TwoPhaseFlowPhaseField", 3)

parameters.name: Turbulence model
parameters.description: Any RANS-EVM model with wall functions or automatic treatment.

parameters.name: Phase field parameters
parameters.description: Interface thickness ε_pf and mobility tuning χ in Phase Field Model.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module.

tools.name: Two-Phase Flow, Phase Field (Multiphysics Coupling)
tools.description: Coupling feature that supplies phase-field-averaged density and viscosity to the flow interface, adds the chemical-potential-based surface tension force, and transports the phase field with the flow velocity. It is the phase-field counterpart of the level set coupling and is used for droplet breakup, coalescence, capillary flows and coating processes.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Two-Phase Flow, Phase Field; Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("tpf1", "TwoPhaseFlowPhaseField", 3)

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Fluid flow and Phase field (pf).

parameters.name: Fluid 1 / Fluid 2 properties
parameters.description: Material, Multiphase Material or user-defined; non-Newtonian models available.

parameters.name: Surface tension coefficient
parameters.description: Defined in the coupling (library or user) and passed to the Phase Field Model.

tools.notes: Verified type string TwoPhaseFlowPhaseField. Phase field is often more robust than level set when topological changes occur.

tools.name: Level Set Model (Level Set)
tools.description: Default domain node of the Level Set interface adding the conservative or nonconservative level set transport equation with reinitialization. The reinitialization parameter γ (about the maximum flow speed) and the interface thickness parameter ε_ls (default ls.ep_default, proportional to element size) control stability and sharpness; the convecting velocity comes from the flow interface or a user expression.
tools.usage: Level Set (ls) > Level Set Model (lsm1); Java: physics("ls").feature("lsm1")

parameters.name: Reinitialization parameter γ
parameters.description: Default 1 m/s; choose close to the maximum velocity magnitude.

parameters.name: Interface thickness ε_ls
parameters.description: Default ls.ep_default (half the typical element size).

parameters.name: Velocity field u
parameters.description: From the coupled flow interface or user defined.

tools.notes: Too small γ lets the interface thicken, too large γ causes mass loss and small time steps. Also standalone for moving-boundary problems (Mathematics > Moving Interface).

tools.name: Level Set in Porous Media (ls)
tools.description: Variant of the Level Set interface whose default Porous Medium node (with Level Set Model and Porous Matrix subnodes) accounts for porosity in the interface transport equation. Combined with the Brinkman Equations it models resin transfer molding, infiltration and filling of porous preforms where the front position matters.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Mathematics > Moving Interface > Level Set in Porous Media; Java: physics().create("ls", "LevelSetPorousMedia", "geom1")

parameters.name: Porous Medium / Level Set Model (lsmp)
parameters.description: Level set parameters and velocity from Brinkman flow.

parameters.name: Porous Matrix
parameters.description: Porosity of the preform.

parameters.name: Thin Barrier / Inlet / Outlet
parameters.description: Boundary nodes of the level set.

tools.notes: Available with CFD, Microfluidics, Polymer Flow or Porous Media Flow Modules. Capillary effects inside the pores are not included; use Multiphase Flow in Porous Media for those.

tools.name: Initial Values Fluid 1/Fluid 2 and Initial Interface (Level Set, Phase Field)
tools.description: Two-phase models are initialized with two Initial Values nodes, one specifying Fluid 1 (φ = 0) and the other Fluid 2 (φ = 1) on different domains; the initial interface is then automatically placed on the interior boundaries between them and smoothed by the Phase Initialization step. An explicit Initial Interface boundary node can also mark the interface.
tools.usage: Level Set / Phase Field > Initial Values (init1: Fluid 1) and Initial Values, Fluid 2 (initfluid2); Boundaries > Initial Interface (InitialInterface)

parameters.name: Specify phase
parameters.description: Fluid 1 (φ = 0) or Fluid 2 (φ = 1) per domain.

parameters.name: Initial Interface
parameters.description: Boundary selection defining the zero-distance surface.

parameters.name: User defined
parameters.description: Smooth initialization is not applied in domains with user-defined initial values.

tools.notes: Draw the initial liquid region as a separate domain in the geometry so that the initialization works.

tools.name: Phase Field Model (Phase Field in Fluids)
tools.description: Default domain node of the Phase Field in Fluids interface adding the Cahn–Hilliard equations for the phase field variable φ and mixing energy density ψ. It defines the surface tension coefficient, the interface thickness ε_pf and the mobility tuning parameter χ, and can include additional free-energy sources.
tools.usage: Phase Field in Fluids (pf) > Phase Field Model (pfm1); Java: physics("pf").feature("pfm1").set("epsilon_pf", ...)

parameters.name: sigma / sigma_src
parameters.description: Surface tension coefficient (from the coupling spf.sigma or user defined).

parameters.name: epsilon_pf
parameters.description: Interface thickness parameter, default pf.ep_default.

parameters.name: chiOption / chi / U
parameters.description: Mobility tuning: user defined χ (default 1 m·s/kg) or calculated from expected interface velocity U.

parameters.name: dfdphi
parameters.description: Additional free-energy source term.

tools.notes: Property names verified in COMSOL 6.4. Keep χ large enough to maintain a constant interface thickness but not so large that the interface is overdamped.

tools.name: Ternary Phase Field (terpf)
tools.description: Moving-interface interface for three immiscible phases solving two Cahn–Hilliard-type equations for the phase fields φA and φB and their generalized chemical potentials; the third volume fraction follows from the sum being one. Interface positions minimize the free energy, so three-phase contact lines and spreading coefficients are captured.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Mathematics > Moving Interface > Ternary Phase Field; Java: physics().create("terpf", "TernaryPhaseField", "geom1")

parameters.name: Mixture Properties (mp1)
parameters.description: Surface tensions σAB, σAC, σBC and interface thickness.

parameters.name: Wetted Wall (ww1)
parameters.description: Contact angles of the phases on walls.

parameters.name: Inlet / Outlet / Symmetry
parameters.description: Boundary nodes.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD, Microfluidics or Polymer Flow Module.

tools.name: Mixture Properties (Ternary Phase Field)
tools.description: Default domain node of the Ternary Phase Field interface defining the pairwise surface tension coefficients between phases A, B and C (user defined or from materials, possibly temperature dependent) and the parameters controlling the thickness of the interfaces. It adds the ternary phase field equations.
tools.usage: Ternary Phase Field > Mixture Properties (mp1)

parameters.name: Surface tension coefficients
parameters.description: σAB, σAC, σBC.

parameters.name: Interface thickness
parameters.description: Parameter controlling interface thickness.

parameters.name: Mobility
parameters.description: Mobility tuning parameter.

parameters.name: Temperature model input
parameters.description: For temperature-dependent surface tension.

tools.example:
// GUI: Ternary Phase Field > Mixture Properties 1: sigma_AB = 0.07[N/m], sigma_AC = 0.03[N/m], sigma_BC = 0.05[N/m]
model.component("comp1").physics("terpf").feature("mp1");
tools.notes: Consistency of the three surface tensions determines whether the third phase spreads (total wetting) or forms lenses.

tools.name: Laminar Three-Phase Flow, Phase Field (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined interface adding Laminar Flow, Ternary Phase Field and the Three-Phase Flow, Phase Field coupling to track interfaces between three immiscible incompressible fluids with arbitrary density ratios. Typical uses are compound droplets, bubbles crossing stratified liquid layers and oil/water/gas separation. Always time dependent.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Multiphase Flow > Three-Phase Flow, Phase Field > Laminar Three-Phase Flow, Phase Field

parameters.name: Physics
parameters.description: spf (LaminarFlow) + terpf (TernaryPhaseField) + TernaryFlowPhaseField coupling.

parameters.name: Study
parameters.description: Time Dependent with Phase Initialization.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD or Microfluidics Module.

tools.name: Three-Phase Flow, Phase Field (Multiphysics Coupling)
tools.description: Coupling feature linking Laminar Flow and Ternary Phase Field: it provides the mixture density and viscosity from the three volume fractions, adds the surface tension forces, and transports the phase fields with the flow velocity.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Three-Phase Flow, Phase Field; Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("tfpf1", "TernaryFlowPhaseField", 3)

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Fluid flow and Ternary phase field.

parameters.name: Phase properties
parameters.description: Density and viscosity of phases A, B and C.

tools.notes: Verified type string TernaryFlowPhaseField (default tag tfpf).

tools.name: Two-Phase Thin-Film Flow, Phase Field (pftff)
tools.description: Multiphysics interfaces combining Thin-Film Flow (Reynolds equation on a surface, edge or 2D domain) with a Phase Field Thin-Film Flow interface and coupling, to track two immiscible fluids in a narrow gap: lubricant/air in bearings, oil/gas in fractures, liquid spreading in Hele-Shaw cells and microfluidic chips. Always time dependent.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Multiphase Flow > Two-Phase Thin-Film Flow, Phase Field > (Domain / 2D / 3D); Java: physics().create("pftff", "PhaseFieldThinFilmFlowShell", "geom1") (3D) or "PhaseFieldThinFilmFlowEdge" (2D)

parameters.name: Phase Field Model
parameters.description: Surface tension and interface thickness in the thin-film plane.

parameters.name: Wetted Wall / Interior Wetted Wall
parameters.description: Contact angle at film borders.

parameters.name: Discretization
parameters.description: P1+P1 flow and linear phase field (good conservation).

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module.

tools.name: Fluid–Fluid Interface (Two-Phase Flow, Moving Mesh)
tools.description: Interior boundary node of the Laminar Two-Phase Flow, Moving Mesh interface that defines the initial position of an interface between two fluids and moves it with the fluid (ALE), including the surface tension force. Because the interface is a mesh boundary, it is perfectly sharp, which gives very accurate capillary and Marangoni forces as long as the topology does not change.
tools.usage: Laminar Flow (two-phase moving mesh) > Fluid-Fluid Interface; Java: physics("spf").create("ffi1", "FluidFluidInterface", 1)

parameters.name: Include surface tension force
parameters.description: Surface tension coefficient user defined or library (liquid/gas: Water/Air, Ethanol/Air, ...; liquid/liquid: Benzene/Water, Corn oil/Water, ...).

parameters.name: Mass flux
parameters.description: Mass transfer across the interface (e.g., evaporation).

parameters.name: Contact Angle subnode
parameters.description: Added by default where the interface meets walls.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD or Microfluidics Module. Mesh smoothing (Yeoh by default) in the Deforming Domain limits how far the interface may move; remesh automatically for large motions.

tools.name: Free Surface (Two-Phase Flow, Moving Mesh)
tools.description: Exterior boundary of a Deforming Domain that is a liquid/gas free surface whose outer gas viscosity is neglected: it moves with the normal fluid velocity, applies external pressure and surface tension, and has a default Contact Angle subnode. It is used for jets, menisci, coating flows and free-surface mixers (Mixer Module) and requires a time-dependent study.
tools.usage: Laminar/Turbulent Flow (moving mesh) > Free Surface; Java: physics("spf").create("fs1", "FreeSurface", 2)

parameters.name: pext
parameters.description: External pressure on the surface.

parameters.name: IncludeSurfaceTension / SurfaceTensionCoefficient / sigma
parameters.description: Surface tension on or off, library coefficient (WaterAir default) or user defined.

parameters.name: Mf
parameters.description: Mass flux across the surface.

parameters.name: Deforming Domain
parameters.description: Definitions > Moving Mesh > Deforming Domain must include the adjacent domain.

tools.notes: Supported by laminar flow and turbulence models with wall functions/automatic treatment, not by low-Re treatment; inactive in Frozen Rotor studies.

tools.name: Contact Angle (Two-Phase Flow, Moving Mesh)
tools.description: Subnode of Free Surface and Fluid–Fluid Interface specifying the angle at which the moving interface meets an adjacent wall, together with a Navier-slip condition that lets the contact point slide. The angle can be specified directly or through Young's relation from surface energies.
tools.usage: Free Surface or Fluid-Fluid Interface > Contact Angle (point in 2D, edge in 3D); Java: physics("spf").feature("fs1").create("cnta2", "ContactAngle", 0)

parameters.name: Contact angle θw
parameters.description: Equilibrium angle at the wall.

parameters.name: Slip length
parameters.description: Navier slip length on the wall near the contact line.

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Points (2D) or edges (3D) where interface and wall meet.

tools.notes: Dynamic contact angle hysteresis is not modeled by default; use expressions of the contact line velocity if needed.

tools.name: Laminar Bubbly Flow (bf)
tools.description: Two-fluid bubbly flow model for low gas volume fractions at low/moderate Reynolds numbers: one set of Navier–Stokes equations for the liquid, a slip model for the bubble velocity, a mixture-averaged continuity equation and a transport equation for the effective gas density. Optionally the bubble number density is solved to obtain the interfacial area for mass transfer and reactions (bubble columns, aeration, electrolysis).
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Multiphase Flow > Bubbly Flow > Laminar Bubbly Flow (bf); Java: physics().create("bf", "LaminarBubblyFlow", "geom1")

parameters.name: Low gas concentration
parameters.description: Default on; valid for gas fractions of a few percent.

parameters.name: Solve for interfacial area
parameters.description: Adds a transport equation for bubble number density.

parameters.name: Reference pressure / temperature
parameters.description: Used for liquid density and gas density (ideal gas).

parameters.name: Default nodes
parameters.description: Fluid Properties, Wall (no slip liquid, no gas flux), Initial Values.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module (or Fuel Cell & Electrolyzer Module). For higher gas fractions or heavy particles use Mixture Model or Euler–Euler.

tools.name: Bubbly Flow, Turbulent (k-ε, k-ω, SST, ... bf)
tools.description: Turbulent bubbly flow interfaces with Algebraic yPlus, L-VEL, k-ε, realizable k-ε, k-ω, SST, low-Re k-ε, Spalart–Allmaras or v2-f turbulence, including bubble-induced turbulence and turbulent dispersion of the gas phase. They model airlift reactors, bubble columns and gas-stirred ladles at industrial Reynolds numbers.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Multiphase Flow > Bubbly Flow > Bubbly Flow, k-ε (etc.); Java type ids BubblyFlowkeps, BubblyFlowkomega, BubblyFlowSST, BubblyFlowRealizablekeps, BubblyFlowLowRekeps, BubblyFlowSA, BubblyFlowv2f, BubblyFlowAlgebraicYplus, BubblyFlowLVEL

parameters.name: Turbulence model
parameters.description: Selected by the interface type.

parameters.name: Bubble induced turbulence
parameters.description: Extra turbulence sources due to bubble slip.

parameters.name: Turbulent dispersion
parameters.description: Gas diffusion by turbulent eddies (turbulent Schmidt number).

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module.

tools.name: Fluid Properties and Slip Models (Bubbly Flow)
tools.description: Domain node of the Bubbly Flow interfaces with liquid and gas materials, bubble diameter and the slip model: homogeneous flow (no slip), pressure-drag balance with a drag coefficient model (small spherical bubbles Hadamard–Rybczynski, large bubbles, air bubbles in tap water Schwarz–Turner, user defined) or a user-defined slip velocity. Gas density can come from the material, ideal gas law or user input.
tools.usage: Bubbly Flow (bf) > Fluid Properties (fp1); Java: physics("bf").feature("fp1").set("SlipModel", "PressureDragBalance")

parameters.name: SlipModel
parameters.description: HomogeneousFlow | PressureDragBalance | userdef (uslip).

parameters.name: DragCoefficientModel
parameters.description: SmallSphericalBubbles | LargeBubbles (surface tension sigma) | SchwarzTurner | userdef (Cdrag).

parameters.name: diamb
parameters.description: Bubble diameter (default 1 mm).

parameters.name: Liquid / Gas materials, rhog_mat
parameters.description: Gas density from_mat, CalculateFromIdealGasLaw or userdef; molar mass Mg.

tools.notes: Property names verified in COMSOL 6.4. Hadamard–Rybczynski applies to bubbles below about 2 mm.

tools.name: Mass Transfer (Bubbly Flow)
tools.description: Domain node adding mass transfer from gas to liquid, for example dissolution of oxygen or CO2 from bubbles. Models: two-film theory (mass transfer coefficient, Henry's constant, dissolved concentration and molar mass, using the interfacial area), a nonequilibrium relaxation model, or a user-defined rate m_gl.
tools.usage: Bubbly Flow (bf) > Mass Transfer; Java: physics("bf").create("mt1", "MassTransfer", 3)

parameters.name: Mass transfer model
parameters.description: Two-film theory | Nonequilibrium model | User defined.

parameters.name: k, H, c, M
parameters.description: Mass transfer coefficient, Henry's constant, dissolved gas concentration, molecular weight (two-film).

parameters.name: ϕ_eq, f_l, f_g
parameters.description: Equilibrium fraction and inverse time scales (nonequilibrium).

tools.notes: Two-film theory needs the interfacial area (Solve for interfacial area) and a species transport interface for the dissolved gas.

tools.name: Mixture Model, Laminar Flow (mm)
tools.description: Dispersed two-phase model solving one momentum equation for the mixture, a mixture continuity equation and a transport equation for the dispersed-phase volume fraction, with the dispersed phase (solid particles, droplets or bubbles) moving at its terminal slip velocity. It is used for sedimentation, slurries, emulsions and electrolyzer gas evolution at moderate Reynolds numbers.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Multiphase Flow > Mixture Model > Mixture Model, Laminar Flow (mm); Java: physics().create("mm", "VolumeAveragedMixtureModelLaminar", "geom1")

parameters.name: Dispersed phase
parameters.description: Solid particles (default) or Liquid droplets/bubbles.

parameters.name: Slip model
parameters.description: Homogeneous flow, Hadamard–Rybczynski, Schiller–Naumann, Haider–Levenspiel or user defined.

parameters.name: Solve for interfacial area
parameters.description: Adds a number density equation for mass transfer.

parameters.name: Default nodes
parameters.description: Mixture Properties (mp1), Wall, Mixture Continuity, Initial Values.

tools.notes: In 6.4 the Java id is VolumeAveragedMixtureModelLaminar; the older LaminarMixtureModel id is kept only for backward compatibility. Requires the CFD Module.

tools.name: Mixture Model, Turbulent Flow (mm)
tools.description: Turbulent versions of the mixture model with Algebraic yPlus, L-VEL, k-ε, realizable k-ε, k-ω, SST, low-Re k-ε, Spalart–Allmaras or v2-f turbulence, including turbulent dispersion of the dispersed phase. Used for clarifiers, cyclones, slurry pipelines and stirred suspensions.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Multiphase Flow > Mixture Model > Mixture Model, k-ε (etc.); Java ids VolumeAveragedMixtureModelkeps, ...komega, ...SST, ...Realizablekeps, ...LowRekeps, ...SA, ...v2f, ...AlgebraicYplus, ...LVEL

parameters.name: Turbulence model
parameters.description: By interface type.

parameters.name: Mixture viscosity model
parameters.description: Krieger type (max packing φmax, default 0.62) or user defined.

parameters.name: Turbulent dispersion
parameters.description: Dispersion of the volume fraction by turbulent eddies.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. The Phase Transport Mixture Model interfaces are the newer, multi-phase-capable alternative.

tools.name: Mixture Properties and Slip Models (Mixture Model)
tools.description: Domain node of the Mixture Model interfaces with continuous- and dispersed-phase materials, particle/droplet diameter (and sphericity for Haider–Levenspiel), the mixture viscosity model (Krieger type with maximum packing fraction, volume averaged for droplets, or user defined) and, for a user-defined slip model, the slip velocity or slip flux field.
tools.usage: Mixture Model (mm) > Mixture Properties (mp1); Java: physics("mm").feature("mp1").set("MixtureViscosityModel", "KriegerType")

parameters.name: ContinuousPhase / DispersedPhase
parameters.description: Materials of the two phases (dispersed defaults to none).

parameters.name: diam / sphericity
parameters.description: Particle diameter (default 1 mm) and sphericity.

parameters.name: MixtureViscosityModel / phimax
parameters.description: KriegerType (φmax 0.62) or userdef.

parameters.name: UserDefSlipVelocity / uslip / jslip
parameters.description: Mass- or volume-averaged user slip velocity or slip flux.

tools.notes: Property names verified in COMSOL 6.4. The slip model itself is chosen at the interface level (Physical Model section).

tools.name: Mass Transfer (Mixture Model)
tools.description: Domain node for mass transfer between the continuous and dispersed phases of the mixture model (dissolution, evaporation, condensation), specified by two-film theory using the interfacial area, a nonequilibrium model or a user-defined rate.
tools.usage: Mixture Model (mm) > Mass Transfer; Java: physics("mm").create("mt1", "MassTransfer", 3)

parameters.name: Mass transfer model
parameters.description: Two-film theory, nonequilibrium or user defined m_dc.

parameters.name: Interfacial area
parameters.description: Requires Solve for interfacial area for two-film theory.

tools.notes: Positive transfer moves mass from the dispersed to the continuous phase; check the sign convention in the settings.

tools.name: Euler–Euler Model, Laminar Flow (ee)
tools.description: Two-fluid model solving separate momentum and continuity equations for a continuous and a dispersed phase (interpenetrating continua) coupled through drag, with optional solid pressure for dense particle beds. It handles high dispersed volume fractions and large density differences, for example fluidized beds, dense slurries and gas-liquid flows where the phases move independently.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Multiphase Flow > Euler–Euler Model > Euler–Euler Model, Laminar Flow (ee); Java: physics().create("ee", "LaminarEulerEulerModel", "geom1")

parameters.name: Dispersed phase
parameters.description: Solid particles or liquid droplets/bubbles.

parameters.name: Default nodes
parameters.description: Phase Properties (pp1), Wall, Flow Continuity, Initial Values; add Gravity and Mass Transfer.

parameters.name: Dependent variables
parameters.description: Velocities of both phases, pressure and dispersed volume fraction.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. Much more expensive than the mixture model; use it when phase velocities differ significantly.

tools.name: Euler–Euler Model, k-ε (ee)
tools.description: Turbulent Euler–Euler two-fluid model using a mixture k-epsilon formulation with wall functions, for turbulent bubble columns, risers and dense particle-laden flows.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Multiphase Flow > Euler–Euler Model > Euler–Euler Model, k-ε; Java: physics().create("ee", "EulerEulerModelkeps", "geom1")

parameters.name: Turbulence model
parameters.description: Mixture k-ε for the Euler–Euler equations.

parameters.name: Phase Properties
parameters.description: Drag, viscosity and solid pressure models as for the laminar interface.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module.

tools.name: Phase Properties, Drag and Solid Pressure Models (Euler–Euler)
tools.description: Domain node of the Euler–Euler interfaces with the pure-phase materials, particle diameter, mixture and phase viscosity models, the interphase drag model and, for solids, the solid pressure model that prevents unphysical over-packing. Drag options: Schiller–Naumann, Hadamard–Rybczynski, Ishii–Zuber, Gidaspow, Haider–Levenspiel (solids) or Tomiyama et al. (bubbles/droplets), or a user drag coefficient.
tools.usage: Euler–Euler Model (ee) > Phase Properties (pp1); Java: physics("ee").feature("pp1").set("DragModel", ...)

parameters.name: DragModel
parameters.description: SchillerNaumann | HadamardRybczynski | IshiiZuber | Gidaspow | HaiderLevenspiel | userdefCd (plus Tomiyama for bubbles with correlationFor purified/slightly contaminated/contaminated).

parameters.name: MixtureViscosityModel / mucModel / mudModel
parameters.description: Krieger type or user; continuous/dispersed viscosity from mixture viscosity, pure phase value or Gidaspow.

parameters.name: SolidPressureModel
parameters.description: NoSolidsPressure | GidaspowEttehadieh | Gidaspow | Ettehadieh | userDefCoeff.

parameters.name: diam, phidmax
parameters.description: Particle diameter and maximum packing.

tools.notes: Property names and option values verified in COMSOL 6.4.

tools.name: Phase Transport (phtr)
tools.description: Interface solving the averaged volume fractions (saturations) of any number of immiscible phases in free flow or porous media without tracking interfaces; one phase follows from the volume constraint. Coupled with a flow interface through the Mixture Model coupling it forms the Phase Transport Mixture Model for multiple dispersed phases, and with Darcy's Law it forms Multiphase Flow in Porous Media.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Multiphase Flow > Phase Transport > Phase Transport (phtr); Java: physics().create("phtr", "PhaseTransportFree", "geom1")

parameters.name: Phases
parameters.description: Number and names of phases; phase computed from the volume constraint.

parameters.name: Fluid node
parameters.description: Phase densities and transporting velocity (from the coupled flow).

parameters.name: Default nodes
parameters.description: Fluid, No Flux, Gravity, Initial Values.

tools.notes: Java ids: PhaseTransportFree (free flow), PhaseTransportPorous (porous), PhaseTransportFreePorous (both); PhaseTransport, PhaseTransportPorousMedia and PhaseTransportFreePorousMedia are equivalent aliases.

tools.name: Phase Transport in Porous Media (phtr)
tools.description: Phase Transport variant with a default Porous Medium node (Fluid and Porous Matrix subnodes) that includes relative permeabilities and capillary pressure of each phase. Coupled to Darcy's Law it models oil/water displacement, CO2 storage, NAPL migration and wicking in paper.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Multiphase Flow > Phase Transport > Phase Transport in Porous Media; Java: physics().create("phtr", "PhaseTransportPorous", "geom1")

parameters.name: Porous Medium
parameters.description: Capillary pressure model and relative permeabilities (Fluid subnode) and porosity/permeability (Porous Matrix).

parameters.name: Volume Fraction / Mass Flux / Outflow
parameters.description: Boundary conditions for saturations.

parameters.name: Porous Medium Discontinuity
parameters.description: Interior condition between rock types.

tools.notes: Available with CFD, Porous Media Flow, Subsurface Flow and Fuel Cell & Electrolyzer Modules.

tools.name: Phase Transport in Free and Porous Media Flow (phtr)
tools.description: Phase Transport variant with both a Fluid (free flow) and a Porous Medium node plus a default Free-Porous Interface boundary condition, for multiphase transport through channels adjacent to porous layers, such as drying, fuel cell gas diffusion layers and filtration.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Multiphase Flow > Phase Transport > Phase Transport in Free and Porous Media Flow; Java: physics().create("phtr", "PhaseTransportFreePorous", "geom1")

parameters.name: Fluid / Porous Medium
parameters.description: Domain nodes for free and porous regions.

parameters.name: Free-Porous Interface
parameters.description: Interfacial saturation conditions.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD, Porous Media Flow, Subsurface Flow or Fuel Cell & Electrolyzer Module.

tools.name: Volume Fraction (Phase Transport)
tools.description: Boundary condition prescribing the volume fractions (saturations) of all phases except the one computed from the volume constraint, typically at inlets of injected fluids. Each phase can be switched off to use a different condition for it.
tools.usage: Phase Transport > Volume Fraction; Java: physics("phtr").create("sa1", "VolumeFraction", 2)

parameters.name: Volume fraction of each phase
parameters.description: Checkbox and value per phase.

parameters.name: Constraint settings
parameters.description: Advanced physics option.

tools.notes: Use Mass Flux for flux-controlled injection and Outflow at outlets.

tools.name: Porous Medium Discontinuity (Phase Transport)
tools.description: Interior boundary condition between two porous media with different capillary pressure–saturation curves: it enforces continuity of capillary pressure (with an entry capillary pressure) instead of saturation, so that nonwetting phases can pool above low-permeability lenses. Automatic settings are available for two-phase systems.
tools.usage: Phase Transport in Porous Media > Porous Medium Discontinuity (interior boundaries); Java: physics("phtr").create("pmd1", "PorousMediumDiscontinuity", 2)

parameters.name: Automatic settings
parameters.description: Two-phase case: derived from adjacent Porous Medium nodes.

parameters.name: Location of lower permeable medium
parameters.description: Side of the boundary with lower permeability.

parameters.name: Entry capillary pressure p_ec
parameters.description: Per phase (manual settings).

tools.notes: Only applicable when Porous Medium is active on both sides.

tools.name: Free-Porous Interface (Phase Transport)
tools.description: Interior boundary condition between a free-flow Fluid domain and a Porous Medium domain in the Phase Transport interfaces, setting for each phase whether the saturation on the porous side equals the residual saturation, is continuous, or follows other interfacial conditions. It is needed for drying and liquid breakthrough in free/porous systems.
tools.usage: Phase Transport in Free and Porous Media Flow > Free-Porous Interface; Java: physics("phtr").create("fpi1", "FreePorousInterface", 2)

parameters.name: Interfacial condition per phase
parameters.description: Residual saturation, continuity or other options.

tools.notes: Residual saturation can only be specified with a predefined (van Genuchten, Brooks–Corey) capillary pressure model.

tools.name: Turbulent Mixing (Phase Transport)
tools.description: Subnode of the Phase Transport Fluid node adding eddy-diffusivity mixing of the phase volume fractions based on the turbulent kinematic viscosity of a RANS flow interface and a turbulent Schmidt number. It is required when phase transport is driven by a turbulent velocity field.
tools.usage: Phase Transport > Fluid > Turbulent Mixing; Java: physics("phtr").feature("fluid1").create("tm1", "TurbulentMixing", 3)

parameters.name: Turbulent kinematic viscosity ν_T
parameters.description: From the flow interface (e.g., spf.nuT) or user defined.

parameters.name: Turbulent Schmidt number Sc_T
parameters.description: Default 0.71.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("phtr").feature("fluid1").create("tm1", "TurbulentMixing", 3);
// GUI: Turbulent kinematic viscosity: Turbulent kinematic viscosity (spf)
tools.notes: When the Mixture Model coupling is used with a turbulent flow interface the turbulent dispersion is handled consistently.

tools.name: Phase Transport Mixture Model (multiphysics interfaces)
tools.description: Predefined laminar and turbulent (Algebraic yPlus to v2-f) interfaces that combine a Single-Phase Flow interface with Phase Transport and the Mixture Model coupling. Unlike the classic Mixture Model interface they support several dispersed phases (e.g., droplets of several sizes, gas plus solids) and are the preferred route for dispersed multiphase flows in 6.x.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Multiphase Flow > Phase Transport Mixture Model > Laminar Flow / Turbulent Flow, k-ε / ...

parameters.name: Flow interface
parameters.description: LaminarFlow or any Turbulent Flow interface.

parameters.name: Phase Transport
parameters.description: Continuous phase from the volume constraint plus dispersed phases.

parameters.name: Coupling
parameters.description: Mixture Model (MultiphaseFlowMixtureModel).

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. Incompressible flow is not available in the coupled flow interface because the mixture density varies.

tools.name: Mixture Model (Multiphysics Coupling, Phase Transport)
tools.description: Coupling feature linking Phase Transport and a single-phase flow interface: it supplies the mixture density and viscosity (e.g., Krieger-type) to the flow, defines the phase densities and absolute pressure in Phase Transport, and computes the slip velocities of each dispersed phase with slip models (Hadamard–Rybczynski, Schiller–Naumann, Haider–Levenspiel, user defined).
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Mixture Model; Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("mfmm1", "MultiphaseFlowMixtureModel", 3)

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Phase transport and Fluid flow.

parameters.name: Dispersed phases
parameters.description: Diameter and slip model per dispersed phase.

parameters.name: Mixture viscosity model
parameters.description: Krieger type, volume average or user defined.

tools.notes: Verified type string MultiphaseFlowMixtureModel (tag mfmm).

tools.name: Nonisothermal Mixture Model (Multiphysics Coupling)
tools.description: Coupling between Phase Transport and Heat Transfer in Fluids that supplies the mixture thermal conductivity, heat capacity and ratio of specific heats to the heat transfer interface and passes temperature to Phase Transport and to the Mixture Model coupling. The predefined Nonisothermal Mixture Model interfaces add Nonisothermal Flow, Mixture Model and this coupling together.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Nonisothermal Mixture Model; Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Multiphase Flow > Nonisothermal Mixture Model > Laminar/Turbulent; Java: multiphysics().create("nimm1", "NonIsothermalMixtureModel", 3)

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Phase transport and Heat transfer.

parameters.name: Mixture material properties
parameters.description: Volume-fraction-weighted thermal properties.

tools.notes: Verified type string NonIsothermalMixtureModel. Requires the CFD Module.

tools.name: Capillary Pressure and Relative Permeability Models (Phase Transport in Porous Media)
tools.description: Constitutive models for two-phase porous media flow in the Phase Transport in Porous Media interface: van Genuchten and Brooks–Corey capillary pressure curves (entry capillary pressure, m_vG or pore size distribution index λ_p) that also define the relative permeabilities, a power-law relative permeability, user-defined curves, or a capillary diffusion approximation when capillary effects are small. Residual saturations define effective saturations.
tools.usage: Phase Transport in Porous Media > Porous Medium > Fluid subnode > Capillary pressure / Relative permeability

parameters.name: Capillary pressure model
parameters.description: van Genuchten | Brooks and Corey | User defined | Capillary diffusion.

parameters.name: Wetting phase
parameters.description: Which phase wets the matrix (needed for predefined models).

parameters.name: p_ec, m_vG, l_vG, λ_p
parameters.description: Entry capillary pressure and model constants.

parameters.name: Residual saturations s_r
parameters.description: Define the effective saturation.

tools.example:
// GUI: Phase Transport in Porous Media > Porous Medium 1 > Fluid 1: Capillary pressure model = Brooks and Corey, p_ec = 5[kPa], lambda_p = 2, wetting phase = water
// Application Library: Subsurface_Flow_Module/Fluid_Flow/carbon_dioxide_storage
tools.notes: Choosing a predefined capillary model automatically sets consistent relative permeability curves.

tools.name: Rotating Machinery, Mixture Model and Phase Transport Mixture Model
tools.description: Mixer Module interfaces combining the (Phase Transport) Mixture Model with a Rotating Domain for stirred suspensions, solid-liquid mixing, flotation cells and multiphase pumps, in laminar or turbulent flow (Algebraic yPlus to v2-f). They support Frozen Rotor and time-dependent sliding-mesh studies, free surfaces and rotating shafts.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Multiphase Flow > Rotating Machinery, Mixture Model / Rotating Machinery, Phase Transport Mixture Model > Laminar/Turbulent; Java: physics().create("mm", "VolumeAveragedMixtureModelkeps", "geom1"); common().create("rot1", "RotatingDomain")

parameters.name: Rotating Domain
parameters.description: Impeller region and rotation speed.

parameters.name: Dispersed phases
parameters.description: Particles/droplets/bubbles with slip models.

parameters.name: Free Surface / Rotating Shaft / Contact Angle
parameters.description: Additional boundary features.

tools.notes: Requires the Mixer Module plus the CFD Module.

tools.name: Rotating Machinery, Two-Phase Flow, Level Set and Phase Field
tools.description: Mixer Module interfaces combining laminar or turbulent flow with a Level Set or Phase Field interface and a Rotating Domain, so the liquid free surface and entrained gas in stirred tanks and rotating equipment are tracked while impellers rotate (sliding mesh). Typical results are vortex depth, air entrainment and splash.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Multiphase Flow > Rotating Machinery, Two-Phase Flow, Level Set (or Phase Field) > Laminar / Turbulent

parameters.name: Coupling
parameters.description: Two-Phase Flow, Level Set or Phase Field coupling plus Wetted Wall.

parameters.name: Study
parameters.description: Time Dependent with Phase Initialization (initial guess often from Frozen Rotor).

tools.notes: Requires the Mixer Module plus the CFD Module. Computationally heavy: run for several revolutions and average.
